{{Quote|I had never seen anything like it. The Mon Calamari vessel was huge. Our tiny shuttle floated next to it like a bitz bug next to a bantha.|Keyan Farlander|<ref name="XW:TOSG">''[[X-Wing Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Independence''''' was a [[MC80A Home One Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80A ''Home One'' Type Heavy Star Cruiser]] that, under the command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]], acted as the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] in the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Originally constructed as an exploration [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the ''Independence'' joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] after the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Subjugation of Mon Calamari|subjugated]] the [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari homeworld]]. It acted as a staging ground for several hit and fade attacks against the Galactic Empire and saw action several times against [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]], including the Alliance victory at the [[Battle of Turkana/Legends|Battle of Turkana]]. During this time it also oversaw the training of several promising Alliance recruits.

The ''Independence'' was replaced as Ackbar's flagship by [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']] following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|evacuation]] of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], but continued to serve an important role and acted as communications control ship for the Alliance Fleet at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] later it participated in the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]]. Almost twenty years later, it would again see action, fighting the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Description==
===Design and roles===
{{Quote|A crosshatch of structural beams arched overhead, layer on layer of flattened ribbon-like constructions that formed the outer shell of the ''Independence''. I had never seen anything built like this and had no idea even what the building material was. Nothing was square or at right angles. It was a little disorienting.|Keyan Farlander|<ref name="XW:TOSG" />}}
[[File:IndependenceHangar-XW.png|thumb|left|300px|Three X-wings launch from the ''Independence''.]]
The ''Independence'' was a [[Mon Calamari Shipyards/Legends|Mon Calamari Shipyards]] [[MC80 Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]] of the [[MC80A Home One Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|''Home One'' type]]. Costing 150,000,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="SOR" /> the ''Independence'', like other [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruisers]], was unique. Its handcrafted outer shell was formed of layers of flattened ribbon-like structural beams, with no right-angles to be found. The elongated hemispheres on the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] took on an organic appearance from a distance. The ''Independence'' saw its share of combat and this took a toll on the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]], leaving streaks of blackened scorch marks on the hull.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

Originally constructed as an exploration vessel, the ''Independence'' was fitted with specialized [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] and communications equipment<ref name="SOR" /> which allowed it to function as a communications control ship in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]].<ref name="CCG" /> Given the Mon Calamari Star Cruisers' military-grade [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] and ability to carry [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]], it served in military roles for both the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> In the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]], the ''Independence'' was represented by a [[Color/Legends|yellow-orange]] insignia that included a downward stroke on the top left parallel to a diagonal line below that curved inward and ended in three fin-like tails.<ref name="XWA" />

[[File:Independence_insignia_SWA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''Independence''{{'s}} insignia in the Rebellion]]
A series of [[Airlock/Legends|airlocks]] and [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]] were located around the ship,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> which functioned as a starfighter carrier. The main hangars, located one on each side of the ship, could each support up to two starfighter squadrons. Bays located beneath the main hangars could store another three squadrons and [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]] allowed up to three starfighters to be moved between each pair of main and lower bays simultaneously. A small auxiliary hangar bay,<ref name="SOR" /> located near the [[Engine/Legends|engine]] housings towards the rear of the ship,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> handled the majority of the ship's [[Standard day/Legends|day]]-to-day [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] traffic. The auxiliary hangar also doubled as a repair bay.<ref name="SOR" />

As a [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]],<ref name="XW" /> ''Independence'' was armed with [[Turbolaser/Legends|twin heavy turbolaser]] and [[Ion cannon/Legends|twin battleship ion cannon]] batteries&mdash;each type numbered thirty-six, positioned six forward, twelve port, twelve starboard, and six aft. The [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] was fitted with six heavy [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] [[Tractor beam projector/Legends|projectors]] and had capacity for up to 120 starfighters, along with numerous shuttles, [[Landing craft/Legends|landing craft]] and utility vehicles. It could also carry sufficient supplies for two [[Standard year/Legends|years]] and was fitted with a Class 1 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and a [[backup hyperdrive]] rated at Class 9.<ref name="SOR" />

===Operational facilities===
====Pilots' section====
[[File:Independence-Hangar.png|thumb|left|300px|A hangar on the ''Independence'']]
The ship was split into four quadrants, each containing various zones and support services. The ship's starfighter [[Rebel pilot/Legends|pilots]], choosing to be as close to their ships as possible, made use of a section of the ship aft of amidships. The facilities in this section included a [[Flight simulator/Legends|simulation room]]<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> where flight recordings from starships and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] were used to recreate historical missions for training purposes. The [[simulator room]] contained four banks of twelve flight simulators which could each run separate missions or be linked to allow multiple squadrons to train together.<ref name="SOR" />

Additional simulators were located in the starfighter repair bay. Each simulator could be configured to resemble the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] of standard starfighters and shuttlecraft. Scheduled training periods were usually booked via a signup board, but the simulator facilities were available to all operational [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and [[Flight Cadet|flight cadets]] at any time.<ref name="SOR" /> The pilots also had access to a holo film room where they could review [[Black box/Legends|flight recorder]] footage from previous missions.<ref name="XW" />

The ''Independence'' had several rooms used for briefing and debriefing before and after missions. Briefings for large operations and missions involving multiple branches of the Alliance Military were generally conducted in the [[tactical theater]], a sizable room with tiered seating around a sunken pit housing a large [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]]. [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Alliance Special Operations]] tended to conduct briefings in one of the secure briefing rooms on the command deck, but also made use of the pilots' ready rooms on occasions. The pilots had two ready rooms located near each of the main hangars. The ready rooms were equipped with a holoprojector, a podium and seating for dozens of pilots.<ref name="SOR" />

====Other services====
{{Quote|The ''Independence'' was almost like a small city, with various zones and support services roughly located in four quadrants of the ship.|Keyan Farlander|<ref name="XW:TOSG" />}}
[[File:FarlanderMedal.png|thumb|right|300px|The Mon Calamari Star Cruiser contained an auditorium for award ceremonies.]]
Although primarily used as a [[Warship/Legends|warship]], the ''Independence'' had a variety of facilities to assist with the administration of the Rebellion;<ref name="TFP" /> the bow quadrant was where most planning and navigation operations took place.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> Alliance [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] had an office on board and there were several lecture halls located on the ship.<ref name="TFP" /> There was also a large awards [[Awards auditorium (Independence)|auditorium]] that was at least two stories high that presented Rebel personnel with various medals for distinguished actions in the service of the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="XW" />

The ship contained an [[Intelligence Center]], located near the communications center, for use by [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]]. The intelligence center was home to numerous [[Datacore/Legends|datacores]] and [[Computer/Legends|computers]] and was secured by two sets of heavy doors, which were guarded at all times. Entry required both a [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinder]] and passcode. From here, intelligence reports were compiled and used to produce briefings for [[Alliance High Command/Legends|High Command]] or mission planning [[Officer/Legends|officers]]. The proximity to the communications center facilitated contact with Alliance Intelligence agents throughout the Empire.<ref name="SOR" />

The [[Organization for Droid and Machine Abuse]] was based aboard the ''Independence'', operating out of Department 1007 on Civil Deck 10.<ref name="XWA:OSG">[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> The ''Independence'' also had a Med Deck where [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]] and [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] would treat any injuries sustained by the crew, often with the use of one of the ship's [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tanks]]. Some of the ship's medical [[Droid/Legends|droids]], such as [[M4]], were capable of conducting psychological evaluations to assess if crew members were fit for duty.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

===Accommodations and recreational facilities===
The pilots spent so much [[Time/Legends|time]] in their ready rooms that they converted at least one into a lounge, fitting it with holo decks, tables and [[food dispenser]]s. When the pilots wanted something more elaborate than the [[Foodstuff/Legends|snacks]] provided by the machines, they were able to get food sent over by the kitchen staff rather than going to the mess hall. A makeshift bar had been set up in the corner of the lounge which the senior officers overlooked. In addition to the mess halls used by the crew, there was also an executive dining room for senior personnel, which had the appearance of something [[Planet/Legends|planet]]-side with fabric-covered tables and fine crockery. The food, too, was above the level enjoyed by most of the crew, with meals prepared individually rather than in large vats.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

[[File:IndependenceConcourse.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A concourse on the ''Independence'']]
Long well-lit corridors ran throughout the ship, with main corridors wide enough to accommodate five people, lined by iris-like doors and sometimes intersected by smaller, tributary hallways. Hallways, like the design of the hull were not straight but curved left and right along their length.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The interior was originally filled with [[Water/Legends|seawater]], but it was later drained to accommodate terrestrial [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="SOR" />

Several large concourses around the ship were devoted to supporting the crew. The aft quadrant contained [[Lucky Lower Thirteen]], originally a ballroom which, by the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], served as a meeting place for many of the crew in the nearby engineering and administrative departments. One of the lower decks contained the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] section which had lower lighting levels than the upper decks, suiting the Quarren species inhabitants who were used to the dark depths of the [[Ocean/Legends|seas]] of [[Dac/Legends|Mon Cala]], their shared [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] with the Mon Calamari. Crew quarters were often simple&mdash;small rooms with a desk, chair, a multi-species [[Toilet/Legends|toilet]], and a cot which came out of the wall at the touch of a button. One of them, [[Cabin 11489]], hosted pilot [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]]. Farlander recorded his experiences aboard the ''Independence'', describing it as a small [[City/Legends|city]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

==History==
===War's end&hellip;and start of another===
[[File:Independence_SoR.png|thumb|300px|The ''Independence'' firing its turbolasers]]
Constructed by Mon Calamari Shipyards prior to the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="SOR" /> the ''Independence'' was one of many Mon Calamari Star Cruisers originally built by the Mon Calamari people for both exploration and defending their homeworld, Mon Cala,<ref name="TEGW" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Calamari sector/Legends|Calamari sector]].<ref name="EAOC Calamari">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Mon Calamari system/Legends|Calamari system]]</ref> For the majority of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the ''Independence'' was away from Mon Cala on a [[Realspace/Legends|deep-space]] mission exploring worlds at the edge of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The crew returned home in the final [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the war to find it had devastated their planet and claimed the lives of many of those they left behind.<ref name="SOR" />

The Clone Wars [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|ended]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] with the Confederacy's defeat while the Republic [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganized]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Having just undergone a refit of its communications suite, the ''Independence'' was still docked in the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] above Mon Cala when [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]] launched an [[Subjugation of Mon Calamari|invasion]]. Carrying only a [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]] crew, the ''Independence'', along with the cruisers [[Defiance/Legends|''Defiance'']] and [[Liberty/Legends|''Liberty'']], evaded the Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] and escaped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]<ref name="SOR" /> before the Empire [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] the Mon Calamari people in the [[Mon Calamari system/Legends|star system]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

Hiding deep in the Calamari [[Sector/Legends|sector]], the cruisers evaded detection for years, focusing on their own survival but taking the opportunity to harry Imperial forces where possible. They eventually joined the fledgling Alliance to Restore the Republic and assisted in the [[Calamarian Revolt|liberation]] of Mon Cala in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="SOR" /> The [[Mon Calamari Council]] initially chose not to join the Rebellion,<ref name="TEGW" /> but the ''Independence'' remained with the Alliance and served the Rebel Mon Calamari [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] after his promotion to the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]]. With its interiors drained of water and converted for use by terrestrial species, the ''Independence'' became the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]].<ref name="SOR" /> During the early days of the Galactic Civil War, it served as a starfighter depot and mobile [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]]<ref name="TEGW" /> and was home to Alliance Chief of State Mon Mothma and Alliance High Command.<ref name="SOR" />

===Expanding the Alliance===
{{Quote|Red Squadron was piloting twelve of those X-wings, stationed aboard Ackbar's ship ''Independence''. I noticed three kills before I had to eject.|Wedge Antilles, ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="IH">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Turkana.png|thumb|left|300px|The ''Independence'' was one of seven Mon Calamari Star Cruisers at the Battle of Turkana.]]
The ''Independence'' was among the first ships in the Alliance Fleet to carry the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. One of the first uses of the new starfighter came at the [[Battle of Turkana/Legends|Battle of Turkana]]<ref name="XW" /> in 1 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].<ref name="Turkana date">As the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] used [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] during the [[Battle of Turkana/Legends|Battle of Turkana]], it must occur after the Rebels' [[Fresian campaign|campaign]] to obtain the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], which occurred in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] according to ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. In [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], the Battle of Turkana takes place before the [[Death Star plans delivery]] to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. According to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', Organa was previously at the [[Battle of Kattada]], which, per [[Empire 5|''Empire'' 5]], was concurrent to the [[Subjugation of Ralltiir]] three [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]&mdash;dated to 35:3:8 [[Great ReSynchronization|GrS]] per the reasoning [[Template:Yavindate|here]], and [[Kattada/Legends|Kattada's]] events thus took place in the preceding [[Standard month/Legends|month]], in 35:2. Since the first two months of a GrS year were the last two of the preceding [[Galactic Standard Calendar]] [[Standard year/Legends|year]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]], 35:2 was in the year before the year [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]/[[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] that was marked by the Battle of Yavin&mdash;1 BBY. Therefore, the Battle of Turkana takes place in the same year.</ref> The ''Independence'' was among seven Mon Calamari Star Cruisers that were supported by two [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|Nebulon-B frigates]], two [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvettes]], and four [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]] when the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] [[Fuel/Legends|refueled]]<ref name="IH" /> in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of the planet [[Turkana/Legends|Turkana]]<ref name="XW" /> in the Outer Rim's [[Pakuuni sector/Legends|Pakuuni sector]] and was attacked by an Imperial [[Task force/Legends|task force]]. Comprising ten [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] [[Commanding officer/Legends|led]] by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Xamuel Lennox]] aboard the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Rebel Dream|''Tyrant'']], the task force [[Space warfare/Legends|opened fire]] on the Rebel ships and dispatched their [[TIE series/Legends|TIE squadrons]].<ref name="IH" />

However, Ackbar quickly responded by launching the new starfighters, catching the Imperial forces by surprise.<ref name="XW" /> The X-wings [[Starfighter combat/Legends|eliminated]] many Imperial fighters and joined Rebel [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighters]] in launching proton [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedoes]] at the Star Destroyers, severely damaging two and forcing Lennox to order a retreat, whereas the Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] survived despite damage to several of them. Imperial Captain [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett's]] report of the battle was included in the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', and [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] pilot [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] recounted in a copy of the tactical manual that the squadron's twelve X-wings had been deployed from aboard the ''Independence''.<ref name="IH" />

[[File:MothmaAckbar-ROTJ.jpg|thumb|right|280px|The ''Independence'' hosted Rebel leader Mon Mothma (left) while under the command of Admiral Ackbar (right).]]
Around this time, the Rebel Alliance was attempting to draw more support to its cause. The ''Independence'' played a major role in this initiative by carrying Mon Mothma to meet with resistance movements on planets throughout the Galactic Empire in an attempt to persuade them to join the Alliance. Security on these diplomatic missions was tight. On one such trip to [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] in the Outer Rim's [[Lahara sector/Legends|Lahara sector]], while Mon Mothma delivered her "[[A Call to Reason]]" speech to members of the [[Agamar Resistance|resistance]] on the planet, the ''Independence'' remained in orbit, deploying four X-wings and four Y-wings, and keeping watch for signs of Imperial activity.<ref name="TFP" />

Mon Mothma's visit paid off quickly&mdash;the ''Independence'' had arrived with a skeleton crew of 1,230 and, despite leaving some advisers behind to assist local efforts, left orbit with 1,233 on board, having acquired several new recruits. The vessel also played host to meetings between senior Alliance personnel, including Mon Mothma, Admiral Ackbar, and [[General/Legends|Generals]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]]. One such meeting occurred in orbit over Mon Cala upon the ship's return from Agamar.<ref name="TFP" />

===Operation Strike Fear===
Following the success at Turkana, the ''Independence'' acted as a staging ground for the Alliance Fleet's [[Hit-and-hype raiding|hit-and-fade attacks]], including several operations by [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Blue Squadron]], [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]], and Red Squadron to counter the Empire's [[Operation Strike Fear]]&mdash;a retaliatory campaign against Rebels in the Outer Rim's [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. The cruiser's starfighter pilots helped [[Battle of Brigia (Galactic Civil War)|evacuate]] the [[Brigia Rebel base|Rebel base]] on the planet [[Brigia/Legends|Brigia]] from the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] [[Invincible (Strike Fear)|''Invincible'']]. Afterward, the pilots oversaw the protection of diplomatic negotiations between the Alliance and the [[Sullustan Resistance]] and [[Raid in the Rudrig system|raided]] the [[Rudrig system/Legends|Rudrig system's]] Imperial [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 units]] to alleviate their shortage for the Alliance's starfighter operations.<ref name="XW" />

[[File:Destruction_of_the_Invincible.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Among the missions launched from the ''Independence'' was the destruction of the Star Destroyer ''Invincible'' using an Imperial warhead.]]
The ''Independence'' later launched missions to [[Capture of the Gafra|capture]] an experimental [[Warhead/Legends|warhead]] and an Imperial [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] that was later used to deliver the warhead to the ''Invincible'', [[Destruction of the Invincible|destroying]] the Star Destroyer to end Operation Strike Fear.<ref name="XW" /> The crew of the ''Independence'' were thus confident about their chances against the Empire. However, they soon learned that the Empire was developing a newer, more dangerous [[Weapon/Legends|weapon]], and the Rebellion launched [[Operation Skyhook]] to discover the nature of this threat.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

===Operation Skyhook===
====Death Star plans====
Rebel [[communications satellite]]s near outpost [[AX-235]] in the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]]<ref name="XW" /> of the Outer Rim [[Auril sector/Legends|Auril sector]]<ref name="EAOC Cron Drift">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]]</ref> intercepted [[Death Star plans/Legends|schematics]] for the new Imperial weapon, named the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. Those [[Satellite/Legends|satellites]] had been [[Battle of Orron III|stolen]] at<ref name="XW" /> the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] world<ref name="EAOC CA">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]]</ref> [[Orron III]] by the ''Independence'' three squadrons.<ref name="XW" /> Due to the importance of the information, the Alliance dispatched [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] in an X-wing to retrieve it. However, his X-wing broke down and came under an Imperial [[Rescue of Biggs Darklighter|attack]] when leaving the Cron Drift. The ''Independence'' therefore sent three Red Squadron [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearheads]] to protect him until a rescue team arrived to repair his ship. Darklighter escaped the attack and delivered the plans to the ''Independence''.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

[[File:Deathstar_blueprint.jpg|thumb|right|280px|The Death Star plans, the capture of which involved the ''Independence''.]]
The plans were later given to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] on her CR90 corvette, the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']]. She was due to transfer to the Mon Calamari Star Cruiser ''Liberty'' but her vessel was interrupted by an [[Assault on the Tantive IV|Imperial attack]], and the ''Independence'' sent two Red Squadron R-22 Spearheads and two Gold Squadron X-wings to assist her.<ref name="XW" /> Shortly after, however, the ''Tantive IV'' was [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] by the Empire near the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

====Preparations for Yavin====
At around the same time, the ''Independence'' launched the Alliance's first direct starfighter [[Battle of the Circarpous system (Galactic Civil War)|assault]] on an Imperial capital ship&mdash;the cruiser's three squadrons targeted the Imperial Star Destroyer [[Intrepid (Imperial I-class)|''Intrepid'']]. The starfighters stranded the ''Intrepid'', destroyed a convoy delivering a replacement hyperdrive, and eliminated its escort before destroying the Star Destroyer itself.<ref name="XW" />

With the loss of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] plans, the Alliance focused its efforts on delaying the completion of the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] by attacking Imperial infrastructure and learning all they could about it by capturing senior Imperial officers and members of the design team. The ''Independence'' oversaw a plan devised by General Dodonna, launching starfighters to destroy the Imperial supply base near<ref name="XW" /> the Corporate Sector planet<ref name="EAOC CA" /> [[Kalla VII]]. The [[Battle of Kalla VII|battle]] resulted in the Alliance's capture of the Imperial Nebulon-B [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] [[Priam (starship)|''Priam'']].<ref name="XW" />

[[File:Independence2.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A ''Lambda''-class shuttle leaving the ''Independence'']]
When the Death Star was completed shortly afterward, the ''Independence'' carried members of Alliance High Command,<ref name="XW" /> including Mon Mothma,<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel base]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] to coordinate defense against an expected major Imperial offensive.<ref name="XW" /> En route to Yavin 4's [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]] in the Outer Rim,<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the ''Independence'' was [[Attack on the Independence|attacked]] in<ref name="XW" /> the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Bestine system/Legends|Bestine system]] by the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer [[Immortal/Legends|''Immortal'']]. The Rebels scrambled all available starfighters to defend the cruiser.<ref name="XW" />

The Imperial attack consisted of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bombers]] to attack the ship while [[Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wing/Legends|Assault Gunboats]] and [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptors]] engaged the defending X-wings and R-22s. Despite splitting up and attacking from three different directions, two of the Imperial [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] groups were quickly destroyed; the third was able to fire [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] at the ''Independence''. The defending starfighters were caught up fighting the [[Gunboat/Legends|gunboats]] but eventually broke away and were able to help the ''Independence''{{'s}} [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] destroy the last bombers. The ''Independence'' escaped to hyperspace with its shields down but with only minimal hull damage, but two R-22 Spearheads were lost in the battle.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

By the time the ''Independence'' arrived at Yavin 4 during its night shift, the crew had already begun to repair the damage, which was mostly confined to the shield coils and some electronics.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The Rebel leaders received Leia Organa on Yavin 4 following her [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|escape]] from the Empire&mdash;she held the Death Star plans but was also being [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracked]] by the battlestation itself. An analysis of the plans indicated that the Rebellion's best hope was to deploy starfighters against the Death Star's [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|weakpoint]] rather than use large ships.<ref name="ANH" /> The ''Independence''{{'s}} pilots and starfighters therefore transferred to the Rebel base, and several of them joined the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], in which the Rebels' desperate attempt resulted in a major victory against the Empire by destroying the Death Star.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

===After Yavin===
====Imperial pursuit====
[[File:Independence3.jpg|thumb|right|280px|An X-wing flying close to the ''Independence'', as seen from an approaching shuttle.]]
After the destruction of the Death Star, the Alliance began to move away from its previous reliance on starfighters to a fleet-first strategy developed by Ackbar.<ref name="TEGW" /> The ''Independence'' continued to serve as the Alliance's flagship and its pilots were involved in several more missions, including covering the [[Evacuation of Yavin|withdrawal from Yavin]] as well as the [[Defense of the Anvil|evacuation]] of the cruiser ''[[Maximus]]'' and the frigate [[Anvil (EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate)|''Anvil'']] when they were attacked by Imperial forces during the retreat from the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]].<ref name="XW" /> Shortly thereafter, a memorial service for Jan Dodonna was held aboard the ''Independence'' to honor the general's apparent death during the evacuation.<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Other missions launched from the ''Independence'' led to the [[Attack on the Red Wind|destruction]] of the Imperial frigate ''[[Red Wind]]'' and the [[Operation Ram's Head|capture]] of an Imperial corvette,<ref name="XW" /> which was renamed the ''[[Ram's Head]]'' and used to ram an array of Star Destroyers and [[Immobilizer 418 cruiser]]s in [[Imperial Drydock IV]] in the Expansion Region's [[Greater Plooriod Cluster]].<ref name="Drydock">{{CSWECite|II|89|Imperial Drydock IV}}</ref>

The Mon Calamari eventually approached Ackbar to help rebuild their fleet. Ackbar resigned his position with the Rebel Alliance and left the ''Independence'' to return to his homeworld. During his absence, Ackbar worked to secure his people's full support for the Rebellion and continued to oversee [[Shantipole Project|Project Shantipole]], the secret development of the [[Slayn & Korpil/Legends|Slayn & Korpil]] [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]].<ref name="TEGW" /> The ''Independence'' was one of several ships in the Alliance fleet to take delivery of the new fighters, which went on to be used in several missions, including the destruction of the Star Destroyer [[Relentless (Sunaj IV)|''Relentless'']].<ref name="XW" /> After the Mon Calamari became full members of the Alliance, Ackbar returned his flag to the ''Independence'' and took the position of [[Supreme Commander (Alliance)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the Alliance Military.<ref name="TEGW" />

When the Alliance was attempting to recruit the [[Habassa]] people of the [[Habassa II|eponymous world]]<ref name="XW" /> in the Mid Rim,<ref name="TEA" /> the ''Independence'' launched missions to rescue Habassan [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] from the Empire and to help a Habassan [[Convoy/Legends|convoy]] under Imperial attack. The operations succeeded in persuading the Habassa to join the Rebellion and the ''Independence'' was chosen as the location for the formal declaration of their support. Security for the arrival of the Habassan envoy was kept tight, with three R-22s from Red Squadron requested by the Habassa to provide protection.<ref name="XW" />

Shortly after the R-22s rendezvoused with the Habassan [[Delta-class DX-9 stormtrooper transport|transport]] ''[[Bardictol]]'', the Imperial frigates ''[[Havok]]'' and ''[[Riptide]]'' exited hyperspace to flank the ''Independence''. Two CR90 corvettes of the ''[[Birkby]]'' group assisted in the fight against the Imperials and the R-22s were able to hold off their TIEs and Assault Gunboats until the ''Bardictol'' reached the ''Independence'' and the cruiser safely escaped into hyperspace.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

====The ''Gamble'' incident====
[[File:RazorsEdge-SWBlog.jpg|thumb|left|320px|The ''Independence'' was involved in a clash between Rebels and renegades prior to the move to Hoth.]]
In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="RE date">The events of ''[[Razor's Edge]]'' occur "two [[Standard year/Legends|years]] since the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]," which corresponds to [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> the Alliance was in the process of establishing a new [[Echo Base/Legends|secret base]] on the remote ice world of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. With the Rebels in urgent need of raw materials to complete the base, the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] arranged a meeting with a [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] consortium on the commercial [[Space station/Legends|space platform]] [[Arnot Station]]. Solo accompanied the mission team, led by Princess Leia Organa and General [[Vanden Willard/Legends|Vanden Willard]], when it set out from the ''Independence'' aboard the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] ''[[Gamble]]''. Among the ''Gamble''{{'s}} crew was [[Kifar Itran]], a secret Imperial [[Spy/Legends|agent]] who had recently transferred to the ''Independence'' from a Rebel [[Transport/Legends|transport]] group.<ref name="RE">''[[Razor's Edge]]''</ref>

Itran revealed the ''Gamble''{{'s}} route to the Empire and the freighter was intercepted by an Imperial [[Imperial Customs Corvette|light corvette]] under Commander [[Degoren]] as it traveled to Arnot Station. When news of the Imperial attack reached General Madine aboard the ''Independence'', he dispatched Rebel pilot [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and Solo's co-pilot, the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], aboard Solo's [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] to assist. With the assistance of the ''Millennium Falcon'' and the crew of the [[Alderaanian gunship]] [[Aegis (Alderaanian gunship)|''Aegis'']], the ''Gamble''{{'s}} crew escaped pursuit by both Imperial and [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] forces and returned to the ''Independence''.<ref name="RE" />

===After Hoth===
====Further plans====
[[File:Independence4.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The ''Independence'' under attack from Imperial forces]]
The Rebels were forced to abandon their base on Hoth when it was [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|attacked]] by [[Death Squadron/Legends|Imperial forces]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" /> Afterward, the flag was transferred to the Mon Calamari Star Cruiser [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']],<ref name="SOR" /> which served as Ackbar's command ship and the Alliance's mobile headquarters.<ref name="DB Mon Cal">{{DB|starship|moncalamaristarcruiser|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser}}</ref> The ''Independence'' continued to be an important part of the fleet.<ref name="XWA" />

When the Empire began working on a [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], the Alliance captured an Imperial computer containing data on the project and took it to the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] colony on the world [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]] to be decrypted. When they were later forced to [[Battle of Kothlis|evacuate]]<ref name="XWA" /> around 3.5 ABY,<ref name="NEC" />, the corvette [[Razor (CR90 corvette)|''Razor'']] was scheduled to rendezvous with the ''Independence'', led by Admiral Ackbar, to transfer the computer's data. Although the ''Razor'' was destroyed, the computer reached the [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser]] [[Mercury (Dreadnaught-class)|''Mercury'']], which took it to the rendezvous point.<ref name="XWA" />

The transfer was interrupted by the arrival of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. The [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|dreadnought]] fired upon both ships and launched TIE Bombers. A group of X-wings sent from the ''Liberty'' quickly moved to intercept and were soon joined by [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptors]] launched by the ''Independence''. The Rebel fighters were able to hold off the TIEs until the transfer was complete and both the ''Independence'' and the ''Mercury'' escaped to hyperspace.<ref name="XWA" />

====Defenders of the Empire====
[[File:Stele4.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A Missile Boat piloted by Maarek Stele attacked the pirate TIE Defenders and later the ''Independence''.]]
At some point around 3.5 ABY,<ref name="NEC" /> the [[Nami]] pirate [[Ali Tarrak]] acquired a prototype [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]] and, after the Nami began manufacturing the starfighters, she entered supply negotiations with the Rebellion. Following the negotiations' conclusion, the ''Independence'' traveled to Tarrak's [[Deep Space Manufacturing Facility]] alongside the [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruisers]] ''[[Lonsigar 1]]'' and ''[[Lonsigar 2]]''. They exited hyperspace to find the facility under [[Capture of Ali Tarrak|attack]] from the Star Destroyer ''[[Grey Wolf]]''.<ref name="DOE">''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter: Defender of the Empire]]''</ref>

The Imperials were commanded by Admiral [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] "Thrawn," and the Imperial [[TIE pilot|pilot]] [[Maarek Stele/Legends|Maarek Stele]] attacked the ''Independence'' with a [[Missile Boat]] until the flagship escaped.<ref name="DOE" /> At some point, the ''Independence'' also survived an attack by the Star Destroyer [[Merciless (Star Destroyer)|''Merciless'']].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|99|''Independence''}}</ref>

===Mustering the fleet===
{{Quote|Gold Group reporting in, Admiral. Sorry we're a little late.''"<br />"''We've been expecting you, Gold Group.|Olin Garn and Gial Ackbar, after Gold Group arrived to help the ''Independence''|audio=GarnAckbar-XWA.flac|<ref name="XWA" />}}
With the threat of the second Death Star revealed, the Alliance began to assemble their fleet near the world [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]]<ref name="XWA" /> in the Outer Rim's [[Brema sector/Legends|Brema sector]]<ref name="TEA" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]<ref name="NEC" /> in preparation for a major attack on the battlestation. The ''Independence'', again under Ackbar's command, headed toward the rendezvous leading a [[Independence task force|task force]] comprising the CR90 corvette [[Saki (CR90 corvette)|''Saki'']], the EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate [[Redemption/Legends|''Redemption'']], the [[DP20 gunship/Legends|Corellian gunship]] ''[[Chandi]]'', and the [[Bulk cruiser/Legends|bulk cruiser]] ''[[Urjani]]''. With the Empire searching for the Rebel fleet, the threat of an attack was high and the ''Independence''{{'s}} group encountered a number of Imperial patrols on the way.<ref name="XWA" />

[[File:Independence5.jpg|thumb|right|320px|The ''Independence'' prepares to enter hyperspace.]]
For the final leg of the journey, the ''Independence'' was to [[Battle of Sullust (4 ABY)|rendezvous]] with the pilot [[Olin Garn]]'s Gold Squadron A-wings from the ''Liberty'', intended to act as escorts. However, the escorts were delayed after assisting the ''Defiance''{{'s}} [[Defiance Task Force|group's]] hyperspace jump; by the time the A-wings arrived, the ''Independence''{{'s}} group had come under attack from the Star Destroyers ''Immortal'', [[Protector (Victory II-class)|''Protector'']], and [[Vanguard (Victory II-class)|''Vanguard'']].<ref name="XWA" />

While the A-wings countered enemy TIEs, particularly the TIE Bombers that were launching torpedoes toward the ''Independence'', Ackbar ordered B-wings to launch and counterattack the Star Destroyers. The Rebel fighters held back the Imperials back long enough for the ''Independence'' to escape to hyperspace, after first ensuring that the rest of the group was safely away.<ref name="XWA" />

===Battle of Endor===
With the ''Independence'' and the ''Defiance'' having safely arrived at the rallying point, the Alliance was ready to [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]] the Death Star.<ref name="XWA" /> The stolen computer data revealed that the Death Star was being constructed in orbit of the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]],<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> in the Outer Rim's [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].<ref name="TEA" /> Furthermore, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself was overseeing its final stages of construction. The Rebellion planned to destroy the station's [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]] from within with small ships while the rest of the fleet engaged any defending Imperial forces. Ackbar commanded from ''Home One''<ref name="RotJ" /> while the ''Independence'' acted as the Alliance's fleet communications control center.<ref name="CCG" />

Upon emerging from hyperspace, the Rebel fleet was forced between an Imperial fleet led by the ''Executor'' and a fully operational Death Star. Alliance forces eventually combated the Imperial Star Destroyers at close range, and the ''Independence'' endured the fighting until the Death Star was obliterated.<ref name="RotJ" /> The ''Independence'' later took on some of the surviving pilots from the ''Liberty'', which had been destroyed by the Death Star, including [[Ace Azzameen/Legends|Ace Azzameen]].<ref name="XWA" />

===Service to the New Republic===
{{Quote|Rogues, back to the ''Independence''. Now!|Rogue Squadron are ordered to break off their attack on Vuultin|<ref name="XWRS22">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 22|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 22]]</ref>}}
[[File:BattleOfBrentaalIV.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The ''Independence'' during the Battle of Brentaal IV]]
In the months following the Battle of Endor, the Alliance [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|evolved]] into the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and continued targeting Imperial locations. [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] [[Scout/Legends|scouted]] the planet [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]] in the [[Bormea sector/Legends|Bormea sector]], and [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] leader [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] resisted his enemies. Consequently, six months after Endor, the ''Independence'' fought at the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]] with Admiral Ackbar commanding Republic forces<ref name="XWRS21" /> from aboard the warship.<ref name="TEGW" />

Ackbar ordered Rogue Squadron and [[Aggressor Wing]] to attack the starfighter defenses, quickly capturing the [[Brentaal Moonbase]].<ref name="XWRS21" /> However, the arrival of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel's]] [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Group]] reinforced the Imperial defenses. The 181st inflicted heavy losses on the Republic, and Rogue Squadron was ordered to break off their attack on Brentaal IV's city of [[Vuultin]] and return to the ''Independence''. However, their feint had succeeded in causing Imperial Admiral [[Lon Isoto]] to withdraw Fel's forces from the city [[Oradin]], which subsequently fell to the Republic.<ref name="XWRS22" /> With their forces on the ground, the Republic forces soon secured the planet and captured Fel.<ref name="XWRS24">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 24|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 24]]</ref>

Responding to the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the ''Independence'' led a [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic task force]] of two X-wing squadrons that searched for stray Yuuzhan Vong patrols to destroy. Near Mon Cala, the ''Independence''{{'s}} task force engaged a Yuuzhan Vong [[Yorik-vec assault cruiser]] and three squadrons of [[Yorik-et|coralskippers]].<ref name="SD" /> The New Republic eventually recovered the galaxy with the end of the Yuuzhan Vong War in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" />

==Commanders and crew==
When fully staffed the ''Independence''{{'s}} crew numbered 5,400 officers, pilots and enlisted crew. During the early Galactic Civil War, the ship operated with a skeleton crew of 1,230 on multiple occasions, including its escape from the Imperial invasion of Mon Cala<ref name="SOR" /> and a later recruiting mission to Agamar.<ref name="TFP" /> The ship had capacity for up to 1,200 passengers or troops. During the Clone Wars, the ship was crewed by natives of the ocean world Mon Cala. Both the Mon Calamari and Quarren were aquatic species and the ''Independence'' was originally filled with water. After joining the Rebel Alliance, the ship was drained to support<ref name="SOR" /> a crew drawn from several species from across the galaxy. Joining the many Mon Calamari and Quarren on board were representatives of a number of species, including [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and Sullustans.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

The crew worked in shifts, with time synchronized with the light and dark cycles of the ship's most recent planetary call. Despite these concessions, areas inhabited primarily by Quarren crew maintained low lighting to simulate the deep waters of their homeworld. The crew was divided into several departments including Operations, Communications, Logistics, Sector Command and Intelligence, with each responsible for just part of the ship's operation.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The ''Independence'' was often used as a first assignment for top prospects among newly recruited officers.<ref name="CCG" />

===Alliance High Command===
[[File:Independence-Ackbar.png|thumb|right|300px|Admiral Ackbar commanding the ''Independence'']]
As the flagship of the Alliance fleet prior to the Battle of Hoth, the ''Independence'' served as home to Alliance High Command, including Chief of State Mon Mothma,<ref name="SOR" /> General Crix Madine<ref name="RE" /> of [[Rebel Alliance Special Forces]],<ref name="NEGC" /> General Jan Dodonna of [[Starfighter Command (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Starfighter Command]]<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and General [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] of Alliance Intelligence.<ref name="SOR" /> The High Command members' staff were also based aboard the ship, including Mon Mothma's [[Aide/Legends|aide]] [[Lynia Delline]]<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[D6-L5]],<ref name="TFP" /> and [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|Lieutenant Commander]] [[Lagrane]], one of General Dodonna's staff officers.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> During the early Galactic Civil War, the ''Independence'' was under the command of Admiral Gial Ackbar, commander of the Alliance's [[Rebel Fleet Command/Legends|Fleet Command]]<ref name="XWA" /> and later Supreme Commander of the Alliance Military.<ref name="TEGW" /> Among those serving under Ackbar was the ship's Sullustan navigator, Lieutenant Commander [[Chiithii'n]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

===Starfighter Command===
Starfighter Command maintained a large presence on board and General Dodonna was frequently on the ''Independence''.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The ship's complement of 120 starfighters<ref name="SOR" /> were manned by pilots from several squadrons, including Red Squadron, Blue Squadron and Gold Squadron prior to the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> Rogue Squadron were also based aboard the ''Independence'' for periods in 2 ABY<ref name="RE" /> and again in 4 ABY.<ref name="XWRS21" /><ref name="NEC" /> Senior pilots stationed aboard the ship included Commanders [[Hamo Blastwell]] and Keyan Farlander of Red Squadron and Captain [[Ernek Marskan]] of Blue Squadron.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

[[File:FarlanderLegacy.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Keyan Farlander was among the many pilots stationed aboard the Rebel warship.]]
In addition to the pilots themselves, the ''Independence'' was home to a number of support staff including the [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] who maintained and repaired the starfighters and the astromech droids that helped to operate them. Senior pilots frequently participated in mission planning, but Starfighter Command also had dedicated mission planning officers aboard the ''Independence'', among them Commander [[H. S'man|S'man]], while Lieutenant Commander Lagrane also served as debriefing officer. Starfighter Command also had some civilian staff on board, among them the retired pilot [[Halley Kadorto]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

The ''Independence'' served as a training ground for Alliance starfighter pilots. The senior officer in charge of overseeing their training around the time of the Battle of Yavin was Commander [[Wex Dafid|Wex "TIE-Die" Dafid]], but veteran pilots also served as liaison officers to rookies to help with their orientation. The high attrition rate among rookie pilots led to the senior pilots adopting the slang term "[[LTS|likely to survive]]" to describe promising cadets. Among the new recruits trained on the ''Independence'' were; from Agamar, Keyan Farlander, [[Sunnar Jan-lo]], [['Ndranth Poussan]] and [[Breth Gart]], from [[Bestine IV/Legends|Bestine IV]]; [[Namrhe]],<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and from [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]]; [[Grizz Frix/Legends|Grizz Frix]].<ref name="DB Grizz Frix">{{DB|character|grizzfrix|Frix, Grizz}}</ref>

===Additional personnel===
Several staff were based aboard the ''Independence'' to oversee recruitment efforts, including Captain [[Beme]].<ref name="TFP" /> General Cracken operated a major intelligence center on board the ''Independence'' which was staffed by numerous intelligence officers and droids.<ref name="SOR" /> Alliance Intelligence also conducted training aboard the ''Independence''; Sunnar Jan-lo was one such trainee and underwent intelligence training while serving as an active pilot before ultimately switching roles.<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> The ship also carried Alliance Special Operations<ref name="SOR" /> and Alliance Special Forces personnel, among them the commandos of [[Storm Unit (team)|Storm Unit]].<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> Alliance [[Ordnance and Supply/Legends|Ordnance and Supply]] also maintained a presence on board, frequently supplying the deck officers who stood watch over the auxiliary docking bay.<ref name="SOR" /> The ship had a number of clerks and [[Petty Officer/Legends|petty officers]] who were responsible for controlling outside communications.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

The ''Independence''{{'s}} Med Deck was crewed by a mix of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] doctors and orderlies, and medical droids, including M4. Other members of the crew included the kitchen staff, a computer operations team<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and [[Resinn]], who led the prosecution of the [[Hurrim]] leader [[Golov Nakhym]] after his capture by Alliance forces.<ref name="XWA" /> The Organization for Droid and Machine Abuse was also based aboard the ship.<ref name="XWA:OSG" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''Star Wars: X-Wing''===
[[File:IndependenceFuneral.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A funeral takes place in a hangar on the ''Independence''.]]
The ''Independence'' was created for the [[1993]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]<ref name="XW" /> and simultaneously also appearing in ''[[The Farlander Papers]]'', a companion book found in the game's "Limited Edition" release.<ref name="TFP" /> The game uses the main concourse on the ''Independence'' to allow the player to select their game mode, with each door representing a different option. When the player selects a campaign, they are shown transferring to the ''Defiance'' from which the missions launch.<ref name="XW" /> However, the narrative sections of the strategy book ''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'' which accompanied ''X-Wing'' confirm that the player character, Keyan Farlander, serves on the ''Independence'' and all but a handful of missions are launched from it.<ref name="XW:TOSG" />

The ninety-ninth issue of the [[Wikipedia:Computer Gaming World|''Computer Gaming World'']] magazine, released in [[October]] [[1992]], featured a preview of ''Star Wars: X-Wing'' that described transitions between missions taking place on the Mon Calamari Star Cruiser ''Dreadnought'' and at a Calamari space port.<ref name="CGW99">{{BookCite|author=[[Wikipedia:Alan Emrich|Alan Emrich]]|container=''X-Wing'' Sneak Preview|title=[[Wikipedia:Computer Gaming World|''Computer Gaming World'' 99]]|date=[[October]] [[1992]]|quote=These transitions between scenes take place not on the Tiger's Claw, but on the Calamari Star Cruiser, Dreadnought and at a Calamari space port.}}</ref> These are respectively replaced by the ''Independence'' and the ''Defiance'' in the published game.<ref name="XW" />

The ''Independence''{{'s}} involvement in the Battle of Turkana is shown in the opening cutscene to the original [[Wikipedia:MS-DOS|DOS]] version of ''Star Wars: X-Wing''. The [[1998]] re-release of ''X-Wing'' for [[Wikipedia:Windows 98|Windows 98]] featured some changes to cutscenes, including a shorter version of the opening cutscene which no longer identifies the ''Independence'' by name, but still shows Admiral Ackbar commanding the battle from it.<ref name="XW" /> The [[2014]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] confirms that the ''Independence'' was under Ackbar's command during the battle.<ref name="IH" />

===Inconsistencies===
Due to a limitation in lengths of ship names, the ''Independence'' appears in the ''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter: Defender of the Empire]]'' mission "Eliminate TIE Defender Factory" as the ''Independenc'',<ref name="DOE" /> though ''[[TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide]]'' uses the full name in its walkthrough of the mission. The destruction of the ''Independence'' is listed as a bonus goal for the mission. The mission's walkthrough in ''TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide'' describes the ''Independence''{{'s}} destruction by Maarek Stele,<ref name="TF:TOSG">''[[TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> but this is inconsistent with its appearance in sources set after the events of ''TIE Fighter''.<ref name="SD" /><ref name="XWA" />

===Class and appearance===
[[File:HomeOneModel-MOROTJ.jpg|thumb|left|320px|The ''Independence''{{'s}} appearance is based upon the ''Home One'' model originally built for ''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi''.]]
The Battle of Endor in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], features three different models of Mon Calamari Cruiser: the MC80 ''Home One'' type, the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 ''Liberty'' type]] and a wingless variant of the ''Liberty'' type later identified as the [[MC80a Star Cruiser]].<ref name="EGWE12">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/25364458982/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-12|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 12}}</ref> The film also identifies the Rebel flagship by the name ''Home One''.<ref name="RotJ" /> The appearance of ''Independence'' in the cutscenes of ''Star Wars: X-Wing'' is based on the ''Home One'' type model and its position as Rebel flagship in the game led to some confusion among fans as to whether it and ''Home One'' were the same ship.<ref name="SWTC">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/swtc/mcc.html|text=Warships of the Mon Calamari|author=[[Curtis Saxton]]|date=2006-10-28|work=Star Wars Technical Commentaries|archivedate=20170605233418}}</ref><ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=threads/7948825|board=Literature|thread=Home One/Independence same ship?|archivedate=20180122171803}}</ref> Both the Q&A section on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="TOS">{{SWArchive|url=qa/?cat=389|text=Star Wars Questions & Answers}}</ref> and the "[[Star Wars Q&A|Ask the Master]]" article in the [[Star Wars Insider 78|seventy-eighth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine confirm that the vessels were two different ships sharing the same design.<ref name="Insider78">{{InsiderCite|78|Star Wars Q&A|Ask the Master}}</ref> Other sources to confirm that the two are different ships include the [[Death Star II Limited|''Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Death Star II Limited'']] set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]], released in [[2000]],<ref name="CCG" /><ref name="CCG2">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Home One}}</ref> and ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'', which has separate entries for both ships. Both sources confirmed that the ''Independence'' served as the communications control ship during the Battle of Endor<ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|54|''Home One''}}</ref> and its participation in the battle was depicted in ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''.<ref name="XWA" />

''Star Wars: X-Wing'' only includes one variant of Mon Calamari Star Cruiser, which is identified in the game's Tech Room as the MC80a.<ref name="XW" /> ''Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance'' features both the ''Home One'' type and ''Liberty'' type cruisers but also identifies the ''Home One'' type, to which the ''Independence'' belongs, as the MC80a.<ref name="XWA" /> The ''Independence'' is also identified as an MC80a in its entry in ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'',<ref name="CSWE" /> which also uses this designation for ''Home One''.<ref name="CSWE2" /> The [[2007]] [[Saga Edition]] of [[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'']] formally established the ''Home One'' type and ''Liberty'' type as variants of the MC80 Star Cruiser<ref name="SotG">[[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'', Saga Edition]]</ref> and [[2012]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' clarified that the MC80a correctly applies to the wingless variant of the ''Liberty'' type seen in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="TEGW" /><ref name="EGWE12" /> The [[2015]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]'' explicitly identifies the ''Independence'' as ''Home One'' type.<ref name="SOR" />

Images of the ''Home One'' model, which was originally designed for ''Return of the Jedi'' by [[Joe Johnston]] and [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]] and built by [[Ease Owyeung]], [[Ira Keeler]], [[Bill Buttfield]] and [[Jeff Mann]],<ref name="RotJW">{{Topps|set=1996 Topps Star Wars: Return of the Jedi Widevision|cardname=Ext. Space&mdash;Rebel Fleet|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75301/cid/6408248/1996-Topps-Return-of-the-Jedi-Widevision-56-Ext.-Space----Rebel-Fleet}}</ref> were used to represent ''Independence'' in ''The Farlander Papers'',<ref name="TFP" /> ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide''<ref name="XW:TOSG" /> and ''Death Star II Limited''.<ref name="CCG" /><ref name="Insider78" />
